name: rpm
description: The low-level RPM package tool: installs .rpm files, queries the package database, and verifies installed files — no dependency resolution.

flags.description: -Uvh: install / upgrade a local .rpm with progress.
Query: is the package installed, and what version?
List the files a package installed.
Which installed package owns this file?
Verify all installed packages against their recorded metadata (sizes, checksums, permissions).

examples.explanation: Lists the first files the nginx package placed on the system.
Reverse lookup: which package owns this binary.
Verifies system integrity — changed binaries or modified configs show up with flags (S=size, 5=checksum, T=mtime).

about: rpm relates to dnf/yum exactly as dpkg relates to apt: the low-level layer that installs and queries, while the high-level tool resolves dependencies and downloads. rpm -Va is a classic integrity check for suspect systems.
mistakes: Using rpm -i for packages with dependencies — use dnf install ./file.rpm, which resolves them.
distroNotes: All RPM-based distributions (Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE uses rpm too, but its front end is zypper).
